title: Transferred model structure on simplicial modules
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, and let $\mathsf{sMod}_\Lambda$ be the category of functors from $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ to $\Lambda$-modules, with natural transformations [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Write $U:\mathsf{sMod}_\Lambda\to\mathsf{sSet}$ for forgetting the module structure, where simplicial sets, horn inclusions, Kan fibrations and weak homotopy equivalences have the Kan model conventions of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Use model categories and Quillen adjunctions as defined in [lem-cbc-dg-presheaf-model-localizations]. Let $N(A)_0=A_0$ and $N(A)_n=\bigcap_{i=1}^n\ker(d_i)$ for $n>0$, with differential $d_0$. The category $\mathsf{sMod}_\Lambda$ has a model structure in which weak equivalences and fibrations are created by $U$. Under the normalization equivalence [lem-cbc-dold-kan-homology], weak equivalences are precisely quasi-isomorphisms of nonnegative chains, and fibrations are precisely maps surjective in every strictly positive normalized degree, with no surjectivity requirement in degree zero. The degreewise free-module functor $\Lambda[-]:\mathsf{sSet}\to\mathsf{sMod}_\Lambda$ is left Quillen. In particular, for every weak homotopy equivalence $f$ of simplicial sets, $N\Lambda[f]$ is a quasi-isomorphism of nonnegative chain complexes.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, §3.3, sequence (1) and the transferred simplicial-module/projective connective-chain model paragraph immediately before Proposition 3.15, printed pp. 11–12. The final consequence uses that every simplicial set is cofibrant in the Kan model.
